title: Why hiding an admin button is not security
subtitle: Authorization must be enforced where data is accessed
learning_objective: Distinguish user-interface visibility from server-side authorization.

source_refs.title: OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet
source_refs.supports: enforce authorization on every request and deny by default

scenes.title: THE HIDDEN ADMIN BUTTON
scenes.body: A regular user cannot see the delete button. They send the API request directly anyway—and the record disappears.

scenes.title: The client is not a security boundary
scenes.body: Users can modify requests, scripts, and local UI state. The backend must verify that the authenticated user is allowed to perform each action on the requested resource.

scenes.title: Default to deny
scenes.body: Check permissions on every sensitive request, including object ownership. Hiding controls is a usability feature, not authorization.

scenes.question: Where must permission to delete a record be enforced?
scenes.explanation: A caller can bypass the UI. The server or database policy must independently enforce access.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Treat every client request as untrusted and authorize the action against the specific resource.
